key_insight: Combining histopathology AI, predicted morphological features, and manually assessed PRAME staining showed diagnostic feasibility but did not substantially improve melanoma discrimination over AI alone.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic—not drug-discovery—study offers a structured way to combine AI scores with established pathology findings, without establishing readiness for routine clinical use.
method: Analyze whole-slide images using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework.
Train models to predict malignancy and established histopathological features.
Integrate AI predictions with manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective cohort of 1,000 lesions, models were trained on 800 cases and temporally tested on 200; malignancy AUROC was 0.970 for AI alone versus 0.972 for the integrated model.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to a retrospective cohort selected for PRAME testing; broader prospective validation is needed to assess generalizability.
paper_title: Integrating Histopathology Foundation Models and PRAME Immunohistochemistry in Melanoma Diagnosis
